To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the dynamic instability of the systems and the "co-presence" of randomness at different levels are a component of the contingent increasing of organization along evolution, due to the presence of constraints induced by (bio-)resonnance and (bio)-entanglement in the networks of co-operation between diverse components.

(i) the living systems are intrinsically unpredictable and their evolution is contingent on the presence and the interaction of different forms of (bio)randomness; (ii) biological randomness is the result of a complex interplay among many levels of organization, which is the source of the unpredictability of biological systems' behavior; (iii) the co-operation among the components of the living systems is the result of the presence and interaction of many forms of randomness, including quantum randomness.
the living systems are characterized by the dynamic instability of their organization and the presence of different forms of "superimposed" randomness.
In summary, our research is concerned with

how to understand the emergence of biological organization and complexity in terms of the interplay between randomness and order in the context of the multi-level interactions in living systems, as well as how to understand the effects of the concurrent presence of classical and quantum randomness on biological phenomena.

the understanding and modeling of the dynamic instability of biological systems as a consequence of the "superposition", at different levels, of randomness and organization, as a component of life's evolution.

the role of randomness and the multi-level interactions in the dynamics of biological systems, with the aim to understand how they can be viewed as an intrinsic component of the contingentially increasing organization along evolution.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the "superposition of randomness" is an essential feature of the dynamic organization of life.
life is the result of a "superposition" between different types of randomness.
the living systems, and in particular the brain, are the most complex, unpredictable and random systems in our universe.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the living systems are characterized by a "superposition" between the classical and quantum forms of randomness, and that this "superposition" is a necessary component of the contingent increase of organization in life.
the dynamic instability of the biological systems and their "superposition" are viewed as a fundamental component of the contingenty increasing organization of life.
randomness is a component, and a necessary one, of biological complexity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
randomness, in its various forms, is an integral part of the dynamics and the evolution of living systems.
the co-presence and interplay between randomness and multi-level organization are a necessary condition for the emergence of life.
the living world can be viewed as a dynamic, multi-level, and multi-scale system that is inherently unpredictable.
